note: Rests on item 1: Gray raised its Q3 political guide 9% and Sinclair its FY guide 13% after Fox last spoke, into a disputed bar whose two sources sit $160m apart, on a name that has bought 5 of its last 7 prints; the Roku/DOJ overhang and the mixed NFL Week 1 ratings (item 9, rejected as no_source but it carries a URL) offset part of it, and the calls-bid skew says most of the up-case is already paid for.

The fundamentals (items 0, 1, 3, 5: top-of-guide Jubilee, a strong Brent path, $50m of quiet 7.01 note redemptions, Tullow's extra cargoes) are real but this name has sold 5 of 5 prints including a Q2 with a production and EPS beat at $108.57 realised (-5.95%); against that sit a near-certain GAAP net loss from the hedge mark (item 2), the Winterfell casing failure (item 4) and a Jefferies cut to Hold two sessions before the print (item 6), so the reaction function takes the sign negative while the number itself is positive.

Close to a non-result with a wide distribution: no consensus, no guidance and no company-level number the market has not seen; the only asymmetry is item 0 plus item 4 (a release that restates ~$6.10/share of cash against a $5.045 spot into 11.6% short interest at 5.5 days to cover near the 52-week low), partly offset by an unknown Q3 ATM draw, and item 5 is right that a rates-driven nuclear sector will probably dominate the window in a direction this evidence cannot call.

The strongest case in the pack: item 0 quantifies a bar that implies only +2% equipment growth after a Q4 that exited at +7.7% with radio sales +40% and +30% sequentially, and item 2 is Allegion printing Americas non-residential up low double digits organically with a raised guide on 2026-10-22, after Napco last spoke and with no estimate revision since; held back from a larger number because this name has sold its beats hard (a 5% revenue beat went -7.7% in the same quarter a year ago, Q4's beat -1.3%), the parts-cost squeeze and the access-control drag are real, and the founder sold 43% of his stake mid-quarter.

A correctly tiny name: 1 of 7 prints up, median reaction 0.99% and max 2.19%, so even the best items here are worth cents; item 2 (AEP, FirstEnergy and Exelon all beating or narrowing up after PSEG last spoke, into an extreme PJM summer) and item 1's NRC full-power snapshots lean mildly positive, the unquantified July storm O&M and the year-end rate-case ask lean the other way, and nothing found is large enough to break a 1% reaction band.
